title: Surgical metrics playbook for LLM cache and eviction
content:
TL;DR:
A compact, operator-focused playbook for instrumenting, visualizing, and running eviction experiments on the LLM KV cache. Goal is to give SREs and runtime owners a minimal, high-signal metric set and trace anchors so cache behavior becomes debuggable and safely optimizable during model rollouts and quantization changes.

Why this doc exists:
- Observability for KV/cache eviction has high cardinality and noisy signals; teams need a surgical metric set to avoid alert fatigue.
- Eviction policy changes (TTL, size limits, LRU heuristics) can reduce cost but risk latency regressions — we need a reproducible measurement plan.

Audience:
- Oncall SREs, serving-runtime engineers, applied-ML infra, product owners running rollouts for model or quantization changes.

High-level objectives:
1) Define 6 core metrics that cover correctness, latency, and cost impact.
2) Provide trace/span annotations to link high-latency tails to cache events (misses, evictions, cold-loads).
3) Dashboard tiling and probe cadence recommendations for safe experiments.
4) Runbook checklist for eviction rollouts and rollback criteria.

Core (minimal) metric set (operator-facing):
- cache.hit_rate (percent): Definition: moving-window ratio of requests served from KV cache to total requests that could use KV. Calculation hint: rate(cache.hits[5m]) / max(rate(cache.requests[5m]), 1). Owner: runtime-kv team. Alert: if 5m hit_rate < baseline-20% AND tail latency increased.
- cache.prefetch_success_rate (percent): Definition: fraction of scheduled prefetches that complete before first dependent request arrives. Query hint: count(success_prefetches) / max(count(scheduled_prefetches),1) over 1m. Owner: prefetch service.
- cache.cold_load_latency_p50/p95 (ms): Definition: latency for requests that required full model-side generation to prime the cache. Tag with model.name and quantization. Use p95 to judge regressions. Owner: serving-runtime.
- cache.evictions_per_minute (count): Definition: total eviction events emitted by cache (evict reasons tagged: memory-pressure, ttl, manual). Alert: sudden >3x baseline for >10m.
- request.path_time_to_first_token (ms): Definition: time from request accept -> first token emitted. Splits: cache-hit vs cache-miss. Owner: api-runtime.
- serving.unit_cost_per_token (USD proxy): Definition: derived metric combining GPU-second attribution and token count (approx cost). Use for safety checks during aggressive caching changes. Owner: cost-modeling / infra-finance.

Trace and span anchors (what to capture):
- Root span: request_id, tenant_id, model.name, route, seq_length, preference_hint (low-latency|high-throughput).
- KV cache span: tags: cache_hit:true|false, prefetch_id, evicted:true|false, eviction_reason, cache_age_ms. Capture timing for lookup and insert operations.
- Cold-load span: includes model_load_ms, priming_latency_ms, kv_write_latency_ms.
- Downstream spans: tokenization, generation, postprocess.
Notes: make sure spans carry minimal PII; tenant_id should be hashed when propagated to external tracing backends.

Dashboard tiling and visual composition (operator UX):
- Top row (rollout health): global TTF token p50/p95, error rate, cache.hit_rate (global), evictions_per_minute (global).
- Middle row (cohort slices): split the TTF and cache.hit_rate by model.name, tenant_weight_bucket (top-10 tenants vs baseline cohort), and quantization profile. Use small sparklines for historical context.
- Bottom row (forensics): trace-sampled tail list, example request replay button (linked to debug sandbox), hot-tenant list with cost delta.
Tiling rules: each tile should be independently queryable; avoid cross-join panels that blow up query cost. Cache-hit_rate panels should be aggregate first, then provide per-model drilldowns.

Probe cadence and sampling guidance:
- Synthetic probe: run a 1q/s per-model prefetch probe that mimics common prompt prefixes — record probe hit_rate and TTF. Run continuously but annotate rollout windows.
- Session probes: sample 1% of real requests for full trace capture; bias sampling toward cold-starts (requests with cache_hit=false).
- Eviction experiment probes: during experiments, increase sampling to 5% for impacted tenants/models for 1h windows.

Eviction experiment design (safe steps):
1) Baseline collection (72h): collect core metrics and probes to build baseline distributions by tenant cohort.
2) Canary (2% traffic): apply new eviction policy to small canary tenant set; monitor core metrics and synthetic probe for 1h.
3) Ramp (10% -> 50%): if canary ok, stepwise ramp with automated rollback on thresholds.
Rollback thresholds (example):
- request.path_time_to_first_token p95 increases > 30% for 15m AND cache.hit_rate drops > 10% from baseline -> immediate rollback.
- evictions_per_minute spikes > 4x baseline for 10m -> pause ramp and investigate.

Runbook checklist for oncall (short):
- If alert fires: check tile "rollout health" for correlated spike in cold_load_latency_p95.
- Open trace-sample panel, filter cache_hit=false and sort by TTF. Look for repeated model_load spans.
- If prefetch_success_rate is low, check prefetch worker logs and recent deploys.
- If unit_cost_per_token rises materially, throttle background prefetch and rollback eviction heuristics.
- When resolved: annotate incident with tenant impact and turn on higher sampling for 24h.

Example queries (promql-like / pseudo):
- cache.hit_rate (5m): sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) by (model) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])) by (model)
- cold_load_latency_p95 by model: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(cold_load_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,model))
- evictions_per_minute: sum(increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[10m]))

Ownership and contact map:
- runtime-kv: owner @Mateo Alvarez, primary for cache metrics and eviction instrumentation.
- prefetch-service: owner @Priya Singh, primary for prefetch_success_rate and scheduling traces.
- api-runtime: owner @Noah Becker, TTF token and request-surface metrics.
- applied-ml: advisory for cohort selection and experiment design.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should tenant_id be included in traces at full fidelity? Current recommendation: hash tenant_id and limit retention for traces containing tenant hash.
- How long to retain trace payloads for eviction experiments? Recommendation: 30 days for sampled traces; longer retention only for tagged incidents.
- Metric cardinality: prefer aggregated metric names with stable labels (model, quant_profile, tenant_bucket) vs free-form prompt tags.

Next steps (action items):
- [ ] runtime-kv to emit eviction_reason and cache_age_ms on every eviction event (owner: Mateo) — target 2026-02-17.
- [ ] telemetry to add p95 cold_load_latency panel per-model to "rollout health" dashboard (owner: Noah) — target 2026-02-21.
- [ ] run first canary using synthetic probe on staging with new TTL heuristics (owner: Priya) — target 2026-02-25.

Appendix: quick reference links:
- KV cache primer (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/KV+Cache+Primer
- Eviction experiment template (jira): JIRA-OBS-4123
- Telemetry PR for eviction metrics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/88

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep the metric set small and unambiguous. Avoid introducing prompt-based labels unless we have strong sampling.
- If cost delta is small but latency tail increases, look at prefetch timing and model load fragmentation.
- We should integrate synthetic probe annotations into the console rollout timeline so SREs can correlate probe runs with metric blips.

End of doc.
